goldens.comment: InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin() recursively calls session.identityProviders().getById() instead of idpDelegate.getById(), causing the cache lookup to re-enter the same caching layer.
goldens.reasoning: G1 is about getForLogin() calling session.identityProviders().getById(), which re-enters the caching layer. C2 talks about wrapped vs. unwrapped models in the invalidation logic, which is a different issue.

goldens.comment: Cleanup reference uses incorrect alias - should be 'idp-alias-' + i instead of 'alias'.
goldens.reasoning: C1 describes the same problem: the cleanup uses a hardcoded 'alias' instead of 'idp-alias-' + i.

candidates: Test cleanup in testCacheIDPForLogin uses hardcoded 'alias' instead of the actual IDP alias (e.g. 'idp-alias-' + i) on lines 381 and 425, so cleanup silently fails to remove any of the created test IDPs, leaving stale IDPs in the realm

registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate compares a wrapped (org-aware) original model from getById() with the raw unwrapped updated model parameter, creating asymmetry in isEnabled() evaluation that can cause under-invalidation - when an org-linked IDP is cached for login, then the org is disabled, then a login-relevant field like hideOnLogin is changed, both models fail the login predicate for different reasons, triggering early return that skips cache invalidation, causing stale cache entries after org re-enablement
